Hello Voaters, I'm currently signed up to take spanish this year. The last time I tried to learn Spanish was in 6th grade, and I did terrible.When getting A's in every other class, I was getting C's. What are some important things to remember when learning a new language? It could also be I was disinterested at the time and never studied (never had to at the time & 12 year old logic of it's just the teachers fault lol.)
What is important to remember when learning a language?

To be successful, you need interest and immersion. You really need to want to learn it and to make the effort to use it in conversation. Try additional education on the side to supplement your class (e.g. Duolingo or other such services). If you have Spanish speaking friends, make it a point to try to speak to them in Spanish (if they're cool with that. Most are). Last, don't let it leave you behind or it gets insanely hard to keep up. Always try to stay out in front with your lessons. Help others that are struggling. It will all help you learn more.

Use it! I know it can be difficult, but try to actually converse with people in Spanish. I didn't learn shit from high school Spanish, but a year at a job working with Spanish speakers is what did it for me.
Don't try to make literal translations in your mind. It'll throw you off if you expect it to have a correlation in grammar patterns with your mother tongue.

You have to accept that you will sound silly at first. Learning a new language is difficult, and the process involves teaching your mouth and tongue to make sounds that aren't always familiar. Accept it, embrace it, and realize that repetition of making those sounds is what helps you to speak more clearly and understandably. You may sound silly at first, but the more you vocalize, the quicker you will pick it up. I wish I would have known this and been less shy in college when I was studying a language. It would have helped me a lot. Also, something to keep in mind is that the best "classroom" is full immersion. If you're serious about learning the language, you should look into your options for study abroad.
Know your parts of speech, nouns, verbs, etc. After that pay attention to idioms. For that though you'll need to find a native speaker or live in country.
You won't learn by sitting and reading the book without doing the exercises. Write it out...
